correctness.rationale: The explicit graph and threshold inequalities hold for every integer \(m\ge4\). For every fixed 0<delta<1 and beta just above delta/lambda(G), monotone iteration proves a positive SIS product-map equilibrium, strict ray concavity proves uniqueness, and a Perron-weighted union bound excludes any endemic fixed point at criticality. Normalized equilibria therefore converge to the Perron vector, whose clique/path block sums satisfy exact eigenvector identities and the proved strict quadratic bound. The analytic inequalities were separately evaluated; finite checker runs only support them.

value.rationale: A recent induced-community epidemic threshold set is proposed as a community-level risk indicator and compared to infection sums. The explicit theorem supplies a natural, falsifiable structural boundary: even for three connected equal-size blocks and while each block is isolated-subcritical, a block with a higher isolated threshold can carry more than a quadratic-in-block-size factor of endemic infection relative to a lower-threshold block. This is a mathematically motivated unbounded counterexample rather than a tiny numerical discrepancy; the construction is transparently nonmodular.
